title: Decimal Fractions: Tenths, Hundredths and Thousandths
seo_title: Decimal Fractions – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify tenths, hundredths and thousandths; convert fractions to decimals; add and subtract decimal fractions. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on decimal fractions: tenths and hundredths from pictures, reading and writing decimals, place value, fractions and decimals, and adding and subtracting decimals. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The first place after the decimal point is tenths, the second is hundredths and the third is thousandths.
  • 3/10 = 0.3, 7/100 = 0.07, 45/1000 = 0.045.
  • To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points and work as with whole numbers.

Examples

Example

2.7 + 1.45

2.70 + 1.45

Answer: 4.15

Example

Value of 6 in 3.064

6 is in the hundredths place

Answer: 6 hundredths (0.06)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 7/100 as 0.77/100 = 0.07 (two decimal places).
Not lining up the decimal pointsWrite 2.7 as 2.70 before adding 1.45.
Thinking 0.45 > 0.5 because 45 > 5Compare 0.45 and 0.50.

faq.q: What does the decimal point do?
faq.a: It separates the whole number from the parts of a whole.
Yes. Zeros at the end of a decimal do not change its value.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth and each full column is 1 tenth. 4 full columns and 7 squares are shaded: 4 tenths and 7 hundredths. That is 47100 = 0.47.
